title: Shopping Offers
summary: Given an integer array of item prices, an integer array indicating the desired quantities of each item, and an array of special offers where each offer is represented by a list indicating the number of each item included in the offer and the price of the offer, determine the minimum cost to purchase the exact desired quantities of items by optimally using the special offers without exceeding the desired quantities.
statement: Given an integer array of item prices, an integer array indicating the desired quantities of each item, and an array of special offers where each offer is represented by a list indicating the number of each item included in the offer and the price of the offer, determine the minimum cost to purchase the exact desired quantities of items by optimally using the special offers without exceeding the desired quantities.
constraints: 1 <= len(price) <= 6; quantities and needs are nonnegative and needs are at most 10.
Buy exactly the requested quantities without exceeding any need; offers may be reused.
hints: Remaining needs completely describe a reusable subproblem.
Memoize the cheapest cost for each remaining-quantity tuple.
Start with individual prices; try every offer that does not make a need negative.
Every offer strictly reduces some quantity, so recursion terminates and caching merges repeated purchase states.
editorial: Every offer strictly reduces some quantity, so recursion terminates and caching merges repeated purchase states.

tests.explanation: One three-unit first-item offer plus one mixed offer costs fourteen.
The first offer plus individual purchases costs eleven.
